'''Marti J. Anderson''' is an American researcher based in New Zealand. Her ecological statistical works is interdisciplinary, ranging from marine biology and ecology to mathematical and applied statistics. Her core areas of research and expertise are: community ecology, biodiversity, multivariate analysis, resampling methods, experimental designs, and statistical models of species abundances. She is a Distinguished Professor in the New Zealand Institute for Advanced Study at [[Massey University]]<ref name="bio">{{cite web |last=Zealand |first=Massey University, New |title=Distinguished Professor Marti Anderson - Chair in Statistics - Massey University |url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/expertise/profile.cfm?stref=204040 |website=www.massey.ac.nz |access-date=30 July 2018 |archive-date=1 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240301011014/https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/expertise/profile.cfm?stref=204040 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and also the Director of the New Zealand research and software-development company, PRIMER-e (Quest Research Limited). 

==Academic career==

Marti J. Anderson completed a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Biology at [[Occidental College]] in 1991, advised by [https://www.oxy.edu/academics/faculty/gary-martin Dr Gary Martin]. She then pursued a Graduate Diploma of Science (Honours) in Zoology at the [[University of Sydney]] in Australia, going on to complete a PhD in Marine Ecology supervised by [https://www.science.org.au/profile/antony-underwood Professor Antony J. Underwood] (completed in 1997). Following this, she was awarded a U2000 Postdoctoral Fellowship to continue her work in marine science as part of the Centre for Ecological Impacts of Coastal Cities at the [[University of Sydney]]. During this time, she also completed a Master of Arts (MA) in Mathematical Statistics supervised by [https://www.sydney.edu.au/science/about/our-people/academic-staff/john-robinson.html Professor John Robinson] (completed in 1999). 

In 1999, she began a full-time academic position as Lecturer in the [https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/science/about-the-faculty/department-of-statistics.html Department of Statistics] at the [[University of Auckland]], rising to Associate Professor in 2007. She was appointed to a Professorial Chair in Statistics at the Institute for Information and Mathematical Sciences (IIMS) at [[Massey University]]'s Albany campus in 2009.<ref name="bio" /> She was the first woman to be appointed to a full-time Professorial position in New Zealand in any of the fields of Mathematics, Statistics or Computer Science.

She became a member of the Professoriate in the New Zealand Institute for Advanced Study (NZIAS) in 2011, and soon thereafter (2013), she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/view-our-fellows|title=Royal Society Te Apārangi - View our current Fellows|website=royalsociety.org.nz}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/a-c/|title=Royal Society Te Apārangi - A-C|website=royalsociety.org.nz}}</ref> In 2015 she was awarded a [[James Cook Research Fellowship]] for work on multivariate statistical models of ecological communities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Search James Cook Fellowship awards 1996–2017 |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/james-cook-research-fellowship/james-cook-research-fellowships-recipients/search-james-cook-fellowship-awards/ |access-date=2023-10-27 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> She was awarded the title of Distinguished Professor by Massey University in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Acclaimed Massey scientist receives rare honour |url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/about/news/acclaimed-massey-scientist-receives-rare-honour/ |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=www.massey.ac.nz |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

Marti J. Anderson is also the sole Director of the New Zealand research and software-development company [https://www.primer-e.com/ PRIMER-e] (Quest Research Limited).
